findings.title: Isolate contexts for client certificate requests
findings.why_it_matters: After a request supplies a client certificate, later requests using the default verification setting can present that same identity even when they did not supply a certificate; concurrent requests with different certificates can also use the wrong identity. urllib3 loads client certificate chains into the supplied SSLContext, so sharing this context across all pools retains and races those credentials. Use a separate context for requests with client certificates so those mutations cannot affect other requests.
findings.suggested_fix: Only use the shared preloaded context when client_cert is None; construct an isolated context with the default CA bundle for client certificate requests.
evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:102-105 -- client certificates are passed as cert_file and key_file alongside the shared context
urllib3 1.26.20 ssl_wrap_socket calls context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile) on the supplied context

findings.title: Preserve adapter-specific TLS configuration
findings.why_it_matters: HTTPS requests through adapters that configure a custom SSLContext or ssl_version no longer honor that configuration when verification is enabled. Per-request pool settings replace the adapter's context, and urllib3 uses the provided context instead of constructing one with the configured ssl_version, so services requiring that setting can fail or use an unintended TLS policy. Respect existing adapter TLS settings before falling back to the default shared context.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the preloaded context only when the selected pool manager has no custom SSL context or other TLS settings that require context construction; otherwise preserve the adapter configuration.
evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:400-402 -- the request-specific pool_kwargs are passed to the configured pool manager
docs/user/advanced.rst:1030-1033 -- documented adapter passes ssl_version to PoolManager
urllib3 1.26.20 PoolManager._merge_pool_kwargs overrides manager defaults with request pool kwargs, and HTTPSConnection.connect constructs a context from ssl_version only when ssl_context is None
